sections.Astrophysical Alerts:
#### IceCube-261123A — an optical transient in the neutrino region and a search for additional tracks

IceCube recorded a Bronze track candidate on **23 November 2026 at 06:54:16.990 UTC**. The revised reconstruction gives an energy estimate of **145.04 TeV**, signalness **0.45677**, an atmospheric-background false-alarm rate of **1.2048 yr⁻¹**, and a direction of **RA 320.45°, Dec +24.58°** (J2000). The 90% directional uncertainties are +1.59°/−1.35° in RA and +1.68°/−1.56° in Dec. [Revised IceCube notice](https://gcn.gsfc.nasa.gov/notices_amon_g_b/143530_34667334.amon) · [IceCube localization](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46345)

On **25 November at 16:05:09 UTC**, IceCube reported **zero additional tracks** in the 90% region within ±500 s, excluding the trigger. The two-day search, from 22 to 24 November at 06:54:16.990 UTC, found no significant excess and supplied no event count. Both searches gave **p = 1.00**. For an assumed \(E^{-2.5}\) point-source spectrum, the respective fluence sensitivities, expressed as \(E^2\,dN/dE\) at 1 TeV, were **0.14 and 0.17 GeV cm⁻²**. [IceCube follow-up](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46367)

ZTF began imaging on **24 November at 01:35 UTC**, 18.7 h after the alert. It covered **5.3 deg²**, or **82.6% of the reported localization area** after chip gaps, to a typical depth of 21 mag. One transient passed its selection inside the 90% region. **AT 2026ahvn (ZTF26accqpcr)** was at RA 320.87190°, Dec +25.37399°, with \(r=19.29\pm0.05\) mag. In the **25 November 21:38:29 UTC** report, ZTF traced it back to **20 October**, when it was at \(r\simeq20.3\). It rose to about 18.6 mag over 18 days, then faded and reddened. Circumstellar interaction in a supernova is a hypothesis that spectroscopy could test. The optical classification and the physical association with the neutrino remain open. [ZTF/GROWTH](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46370) · [TNS record](https://www.wis-tns.org/object/2026ahvn)

#### GRB 261122B — SOAR recovers the afterglow 3.2 days after a softening gamma-ray burst

SVOM/ECLAIRs triggered on **22 November at 22:46:55 UTC**. The team corrected the designation of burst **sb26112202** to **GRB 261122B** on 23 November. On **25 November at 10:49:26 UTC**, ECLAIRs reported three peaks and \(T_{90}=222.8\pm1.8\) s (4–120 keV). The 5–120 keV photon power-law index went from **−1.70 ± 0.12** at +2.7 to +37 s to **−2.37 ± 0.04** at +156 to +226 s (68% confidence). GRM, which triggered at 22:46:54.400 UTC, reported on **25 November at 20:43 UTC** that \(T_{90}=193^{+10}_{-9}\) s in 15–5000 keV. Its cutoff-power-law fit gave \(E_{\rm peak}=58.7^{+21.8}_{-11.4}\) keV and a 10–1000 keV fluence of \((7.15^{+1.22}_{-0.83})\times10^{-6}\) erg cm⁻² from −1.4 to +234.6 s. [Designation correction](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46339) · [ECLAIRs](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46365) · [GRM](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46369)

SOAR imaging began on **26 November at 02:48:26 UTC**. The afterglow was at **RA 3.973846°, Dec −38.828221°** (J2000), with 0.2″ quoted uncertainty, 0.16″ from the reported SVOM/VT position. At +76.79 h it measured **r = 22.49 ± 0.23 (photometry) ± 0.02 (calibration) AB mag**. The team reported the detection at **08:17:32 UTC**. The aperture photometry includes no colour-term or Galactic-extinction correction. A fainter catalogue source lies 0.31″ away. Its host status remains open. An earlier ATCA observation at +6.6 h gave a preliminary **5 GHz** detection of **about 0.2 mJy** at the optical position. [SOAR](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46371) · [SVOM/VT](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46338) · [ATCA](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46351)

#### EP261122a — the X-ray flux declines by at least a factor of 32

Einstein Probe’s **25 November 11:13:45 UTC** analysis places the onset at **22 November 06:09:52 UTC**, before the onboard trigger at 06:12:37. WXT recorded one pulse over **170 s**, until the observation was interrupted. Its mean unabsorbed 0.5–4 keV flux was \(3.13^{+0.99}_{-0.80}\times10^{-10}\) erg cm⁻² s⁻¹. FXT began at **07:17:14 UTC** and refined the position to **RA 49.3135°, Dec +16.4448°** (J2000), reducing the 90% error radius from **20″ to 10″**. [Initial alert](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46331) · [Refined analysis](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46366)

The first FXT exposure gave an unabsorbed **0.5–10 keV** flux of \(3.88^{+2.50}_{-1.38}\times10^{-13}\) erg cm⁻² s⁻¹. A second exposure starting **24 November at 10:21:26 UTC** (+52.19 h) set a **90% upper limit of \(1.2\times10^{-14}\) erg cm⁻² s⁻¹** in the same band. The quoted WXT and FXT flux errors are at 90% confidence. The team infers a decline of at least 32 using the first-epoch central flux. Earlier near-infrared imaging reached **J > 19.93** and **Hs > 19.45** AB mag (5σ). The X-ray fading establishes variability. The source class remains undetermined. [FXT](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46366) · [MDM/MIRAGE](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46350)

#### GRB 261122A — a 93-second burst with a poorly constrained spectral peak

Fermi/GBM triggered on **22 November at 01:32:20 UTC**, and SVOM/GRM triggered at **01:32:22 UTC**. Fermi placed the burst at **RA 271.1°, Dec −57.7°** (J2000), with a **3.7° statistical localization uncertainty**. The position was 98° from SVOM’s optical axis, outside the ECLAIRs field. GRM’s **25 November 20:34:44 UTC** report resolves multiple pulses with \(T_{90}=93^{+18}_{-23}\) s in 15–5000 keV. From −47 to +73 s relative to the GRM trigger, the cutoff-power-law index was \(-1.5^{+0.2}_{-0.3}\), the 10–1000 keV fluence was \((1.2\pm0.2)\times10^{-5}\) erg cm⁻², and \(E_{\rm peak}=396^{+858}_{-187}\) keV. The uncertainty permits a wide range of peak energies. [Fermi localization](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46329) · [SVOM/GRM spectrum](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46368)

#### SN 2026acxa — a late radio limit for a broad-lined Type Ic supernova

ATCA observed the optical position of **SN 2026acxa** on **21 November**, approximately **57 days after ZTF discovered it on 25 September at 05:26:53 UTC**. The **25 November 09:36:15 UTC** report gives a Stokes-I image rms of about **8 µJy beam⁻¹** and a **3σ upper limit of approximately 24 µJy** for an unresolved source at **8.45 GHz**. This constrains the radio brightness at that position and epoch. Earlier or fainter radio emission remains possible. [ATCA](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46364) · [TNS discovery](https://www.wis-tns.org/index.php/object/2026acxa/discovery-cert) · [TNS classification](https://www.wis-tns.org/object/2026acxa/classification-cert)

#### EP-WXT 01709322890 — a stellar flare with a second optical peak

Einstein Probe recorded the X-ray trigger on **24 November at 02:29:50 UTC** and identified **2MASS J01433150+3904165** as the likely flaring star, with an estimated 0.5–4 keV flux of approximately \(1.0\times10^{-10}\) erg cm⁻² s⁻¹. BOOTES observed the star fading in three optical bands from **02:36:35 UTC**. Its circular, revised on **25 November at 14:01:12 UTC**, corrects the observation date from **24 March to 24 November**. [Einstein Probe](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46352) · [BOOTES original](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46353/1) · [Corrected circular](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46353)

KAIT began imaging at **02:42:34 UTC on 24 November**. The star faded from **B = 13.81 ± 0.16** to **15.54 ± 0.06 mag** over 4.8 h. About 95 minutes after the X-ray trigger, it brightened again to **B = 13.84 ± 0.06**, in an episode lasting about ten minutes. KAIT’s **25 November 07:06:27 UTC** report independently confirms the stellar-flare identification. [KAIT](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46363)

source_audit.revision_provenance: Fresh source review from the previous day’s verified cutoff. Supersedes the 26 November 10:44:11 CET alerts handoff. Corrects the one-hour window-start error, includes the ATCA supernova limit and the BOOTES date correction, and distinguishes the track count in the 1,000-second IceCube search from the two-day result. Earlier event material provides context for new reports.
access_gaps: Historical JSON/Kafka notices, retractions and sky maps could not be replayed exhaustively for LVK, neutrino and gamma-ray streams. GraceDB creation-order coverage does not enumerate every log update to older events.

The daily GCN edit archive ends at 2026-11-25T19:38:12Z. Current records and versions were checked for the selected events. Edits after the snapshot to unrelated older circulars are not fully enumerable.

Einstein Probe’s direct VHF, BeiDou and FXT listings returned HTTP 403, including a repeated VHF request. The SVOM French Science Center returned a client-rendered shell. Mission-team GCN reports were available.

No comprehensive public KM3NeT or ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray event ledger was verified. Legacy HAWC/AMON tables are dated. Requests for the HAWC and MAGIC collaboration sites returned HTTP 503, including alternate/retry checks.

The Swift/BAT GUANO queue contained a pending analysis for the 25 November GBM trigger. Direct TNS certificate requests returned HTTP 403; indexed discovery/classification records and the full ATCA circular were available.
